O.content: The title identifies the display as "Top Regions," and the plot shows five labeled regional points.
The only visible quantitative axis inscriptions are "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and "Sales ($ thousands)".

B.text: If a broader budget approval requires evidence of advertising causal impact, ROI/profitability, or complete regional coverage, then a scatterplot showing only spend and sales for the displayed top regions is insufficient and supports requesting full analysis instead.
B.conditions: Applies when the organization requires causal, return, or full-population evidence before approving expansion.

O.content: The printed title reads "Top Regions: Ad Spend vs Sales".
The horizontal-axis inscription reads "Advertising Spend ($ thousands)" and its printed ticks increase from 25 at left to 75 at right.
The vertical-axis inscription reads "Sales ($ thousands)" and its printed ticks increase from 50 near the bottom to 180 near the top.
The labeled blue points Region A, Region B, Region C, Region D, and Region E progress from lower-left to upper-right; Region E is the rightmost and highest point.

B.text: If the horizontal axis encodes Advertising Spend and increases left-to-right, the vertical axis encodes Sales and increases upward, and the labeled regional points are comparable observations, then the plotted ordering indicates that higher-spend regions in this displayed set also have higher sales. Approving broader expansion additionally requires the unstated decision assumption that this descriptive association is sufficient support for expansion.
B.conditions: Applies only to the five displayed labeled regions; it does not establish causality, incremental return, or profitability.
